workflow.title: Lab 5: Workflow Builder & Workflow API
workflow.weeks: Keep-alive slots (10-15 min each); exercise 7 is an optional 30-45 min lab
workflow.goal: Build and publish one small workflow (web form -> signature), then start it the three ways the exam asks about: manually, from a link and from an API call. Drive it through the Maestro API (aow_manage, trigger requirements, trigger, instance status, cancel vs pause/resume) and embed the instance URL, so that the scenario answers about start methods, embedding restrictions and instance management become things you have seen.
setup: Use your developer (demo) account only. Workflows live under Agreements > Workflows (Workflow Builder / Maestro).
Your user needs the workflow permissions: Workflows: Create to build and publish, Workflows: Prepare to run published workflows.
Create a STANDALONE web form (Forms > Web Forms, not derived from a template) with fields such as fullName and email, and activate it. Note each field's Field name.
Create an eSignature template with one signer role and text fields named like the form fields (for example fullName) plus a signHere field.

API calls: Postman or the API Explorer with a token that has the scopes signature and aow_manage. Base path demo https://api-d.docusign.com/v1 (production https://api.docusign.com/v1). Use placeholders {accountId}, {workflowId}, {instanceId}, {accessToken}.

Reference code (read only, never copy keys or IDs from its config): d:/Docusign exam/docusign-node-quickstart/app/lib/maestro/examples/triggerWorkflow.js, pauseWorkflow.js, resumeWorkflow.js, cancelWorkflow.js, and ../workflowUtils.js (publish with isPreRunCheck and consentUrl).
The plan's Embedding lab page at http://127.0.0.1:5173 is used in exercise 5.

exercises.title: 1. Build and publish: web form -> template -> signature
steps: Agreements > Workflows > Create Workflow > start from a blank canvas.
Set the start method to From an API call and add one participant role (for example Applicant) with name and email as start variables.
Add the step Collect Data with Web Forms and pick your standalone web form for the Applicant.
Add Prepare eSignature Template, pick your template and map the web form fields to the template fields.
Add Send Documents for Signature (Applicant signs), then Show a Confirmation Screen.
Save the draft (drafts are not saved automatically), then Review & Publish. Fix every error the check reports and publish.
exercises.api: No API call: Workflow Builder UI. (Programmatic equivalent, for reading only: POST https://demo.services.docusign.net/aow-manage/v1.0/management/accounts/{accountId}/workflowDefinitions/{workflowId}/publish?isPreRunCheck=true, see workflowUtils.js.)
observe: Whether the template-based web form you might try first is offered in the web form step: web forms derived from eSignature templates cannot be used in workflows; the form must be standalone.
The publish check lists errors that block publishing (missing mappings, unassigned participants).
After publishing, the workflow is visible to everyone on the account with workflow permissions.
examTraps: Step order follows the business process: collect data -> (verify identity) -> prepare template -> send for signature -> archive/notify.
Prepare eSignature Template fits when one template covers every instance; document generation fits when content varies.
Publishing is blocked until all check errors are fixed; a consent error returns a consentUrl (exercise 7).

exercises.title: 2. Start methods: manually vs from a link vs from an API call
steps: Duplicate the workflow twice (or export and import it) and set one copy to start Manually in Docusign and the other From a link; publish both.
Manual copy: on the Workflows list open the three-dot menu > Run Workflow, fill in the participant and start it.
Link copy: click the link icon, copy the URL and open it in a private browser window as if you were a website visitor.
Try to find a Run Workflow option or a link for the API-call workflow from exercise 1 and note what is and is not offered.
exercises.api: No API call: Workflow Builder UI.
observe: Manual start asks the sender for participant data, like sending from a template.
The link start needs no Docusign user: the participant who opens the link starts the instance (self-service intake).
Each started instance appears under View Instances for that workflow.
examTraps: Client intake or account change request on a public website -> From a link.
Internal user starts the process for a known recipient -> Manually in Docusign (needs Workflows: Prepare).
Your application starts it, passing data -> From an API call (trigger_inputs).
Editing participants or steps of a published workflow changes only NEW instances; running instances are not modified.

exercises.title: 3. Token with aow_manage, list workflows, read trigger requirements
steps: Get an access token whose scope includes signature and aow_manage (for JWT add aow_manage to the scope of the assertion and grant consent again if needed).
Call GetWorkflowsList and find the workflow from exercise 1 and its id.
Call GetWorkflowTriggerRequirements for that workflowId.
Repeat the list call with a token WITHOUT aow_manage and note the error.
observe: The list shows each workflow with its id, name and status (the quickstart filters with status active).

Trigger requirements return the trigger event type (HTTP), the trigger_input_schema (field names and types, for example the participant name and email start variables) and a trigger url that carries mtid and mtsec query parameters generated at publish time.
Without aow_manage the call is refused (401/403), even though the same token works for eSignature.
examTraps: Maestro uses the same OAuth tokens as eSignature, but the token must include the Maestro scope aow_manage.
Read trigger requirements BEFORE triggering: a wrong or missing input that does not match trigger_input_schema is a classic runtime error.
Maestro base path is api-d.docusign.com/v1 (demo) / api.docusign.com/v1 (prod), not {base_uri}/restapi.

exercises.title: 4. TriggerWorkflow and track the instance
steps: Call TriggerWorkflow with an instance_name and trigger_inputs that match the schema from exercise 3 (use your own email).
Save the instance id and the instance URL from the 201 response.
Call getWorkflowInstancesList, then getWorkflowInstance for your instance.
Complete the web form and signature from the email or the instance URL, then call getWorkflowInstance again.
Trigger once more with one required input left out and read the error.
observe: The 201 response returns the new instance id and a workflow instance URL (the reference names them instance_id and instance_url; the SDK sample shows instanceId and workflowInstanceUrl).
getWorkflowInstance shows name, status, start and end times and started_by; the status changes after you complete the steps.
The same instance is visible in the UI under View Instances > View details, with completed, active and incomplete steps.
The trigger with a missing input fails instead of starting an instance (observe the status code and message).
examTraps: Trigger by API = GetWorkflowTriggerRequirements -> TriggerWorkflow (instance_name + trigger_inputs) -> instance id + URL.
To be told about progress instead of polling, subscribe with Connect to workflow-started, workflow-failed and workflow-completed (JSON SIM only).
getWorkflowInstance needs both workflowId and instanceId in the path.

exercises.title: 5. Embed the instance URL: redirect vs iframe
steps: Trigger a new instance (exercise 4) and copy the instance URL.
Open the Embedding lab page at http://127.0.0.1:5173, paste the URL and choose (1) full-page redirect.
Trigger another instance (do not reuse a completed one), paste its URL and choose (2) plain iframe.
Work through the web form and the signing step in each mode and note where the browser ends up when the workflow finishes.
Optional: compare with docusign-node-quickstart/app/views/pages/maestro-examples/eg001EmbedWorkflow.ejs (a plain iframe with the instance URL).
exercises.api:
POST .../workflows/{workflowId}/actions/trigger (as in exercise 4), then use the returned instance URL:
Redirect: window.location = instanceUrl
Iframe: <iframe src="{instanceUrl}" width="800" height="600"></iframe>
observe: Redirect: the user leaves your app and stays on the Docusign page after the workflow finishes.
Iframe: your page stays visible around the workflow and the user is still in your app at the end, so your app decides where to route next.
Observe whether the signing step inside the iframe opens in classic view (the documented restriction: focused view is not supported for Send Documents for Signature in embedded workflow instances).
Observe whether the browser console shows any framing error for your origin http://127.0.0.1:5173 (the Maestro docs do not document a frameAncestors setting for workflow instances).
examTraps: Embedding is supported only for workflows that start From a link or From an API call; with starting values in trigger_inputs, prefer From an API call.
All step types work embedded EXCEPT Collect Data from an ID; Verify Someone's Identity supports only Phone Authentication when embedded.
Do not embed a workflow that has no UI steps (for example one that only sends an email).
Embedded workflow instance: no focused view for the signature step; Docusign JS is for focused view signing and web forms, not for the workflow instance URL.

exercises.title: 6. Cancel one instance vs pause and resume the workflow
steps: Trigger two instances and leave both unfinished.
Call pauseNewWorkflowInstances for the workflow, then try TriggerWorkflow again and record the result.
Open one of the two running instances and check whether it can still be completed while the workflow is paused.
Call cancelWorkflowInstance for the other instance and read it with getWorkflowInstance.
Call resumePausedWorkflow and trigger once more.
In the UI, try to Unpublish while an instance is running, and note the rules.
observe: Pause returns the workflow with status paused; resume returns status active.
While paused, new triggers are refused but already running instances keep running.
The canceled instance shows a canceled status; data collected so far is kept but no further steps run.
Unpublish is only possible for a paused workflow with no running instances; only unpublished workflows can be deleted, permanently.
examTraps: Stop ONE stuck or wrong instance -> cancelWorkflowInstance; stop NEW starts (maintenance, incident) -> pauseNewWorkflowInstances, later resumePausedWorkflow.
Pause does not stop running instances; cancel does not affect other instances.
A paused workflow still counts toward the workflow quota and changes to it cannot be published; unpublished workflows do not count.
Move workflows demo -> production with export/import (templates and web forms referenced by the steps come along).

exercises.title: 7. Optional (30-45 min): publish by API, consentUrl and runtime errors
steps: Run the Node quickstart Maestro example 1 (Trigger workflow) in your demo account with your own credentials in its config (never copy or print values that are already there). It creates a workflow from a template and publishes it.
Read workflowUtils.js publishWorkflow: it calls publish with isPreRunCheck=true and, on 'consent required', returns a consentUrl.
If the quickstart shows a consent page, open the consentUrl, grant consent, then publish again (without isPreRunCheck=true) and trigger.
Break it on purpose: uninstall or disconnect an extension app used by a workflow step (if you have one from Lab 6), or trigger with a token without aow_manage, and record each error message.
Optional: add an account-level Connect configuration (JSON SIM) with the Maestro events workflow-started, workflow-failed, workflow-completed pointed at webhook.site and watch one instance.
exercises.api:
POST https://demo.services.docusign.net/aow-manage/v1.0/management/accounts/{accountId}/workflowDefinitions/{workflowId}/publish?isPreRunCheck=true
-> error with message 'consent required' and a consentUrl
(grant consent, then call publish again without isPreRunCheck=true)
observe: The pre-publication check runs before publishing and fails when consent is missing; the response includes consentUrl.
After consent the same publish succeeds and the workflow can be triggered.
Runtime errors map to causes: missing consent or scope, inputs that do not match trigger_input_schema, an extension app that is not installed or connected.
Connect Maestro events arrive only in JSON SIM format.
examTraps: Publish fails with a consent error -> open consentUrl, grant consent, publish again (not: create a new integration key, not: change the start method).
Extension app steps in a workflow require the app to be installed and connected in the account (private apps only for the listed accounts).
Going live: publish the workflows the app invokes, make sure the extension apps used are published, and pass Go-Live for the integration key.

cleanup: Cancel any instances still running from the labs.
Pause, then unpublish the test workflows (unpublished workflows do not count toward the quota); delete only the ones you will never need.
Delete or disable any Connect configuration you created for Maestro events.
Remove tokens and IDs from Postman environments you plan to share.
takeaways: Self-service from a website -> From a link; internal sender -> Manually in Docusign; your app with data -> From an API call.
API start = token with aow_manage -> GetWorkflowTriggerRequirements -> TriggerWorkflow(instance_name, trigger_inputs) -> instance id + URL.
Track with getWorkflowInstance (status, times, started_by) or Connect workflow-started/failed/completed (JSON SIM), not tight polling.
Cancel = one instance, data kept, no further steps; pause/resume = new instances only.
Embedded instance: redirect leaves the user at Docusign, iframe keeps them in your app; no Collect Data from an ID, phone-only IDV, no focused view for signing.
Publish runs a pre-check; a consent error returns consentUrl: grant consent, then publish again.
Workflow web form steps need standalone web forms; connected fields are not supported in Maestro.
Edits to a published workflow apply to new instances only; export/import moves workflows from demo to production.

extension_apps.title: Lab 6: App Center & Extension Apps
extension_apps.weeks: Keep-alive slots (10-15 min each); exercise 3 is an optional 30-45 min lab
extension_apps.goal: Register an extension app in the Developer Console both ways (form and manifest), connect it to a reference implementation, and run the console connection and extension tests followed by a functional test from eSignature or Maestro. Finish with the distribution and review decisions, so that public vs private, manifest structure and the register -> test -> review -> publish lifecycle are concrete.
setup: Use your developer (demo) account and the Developer Console (Extension apps > My Extension Apps). Never register with production secrets.

Open the Docusign Reference Implementations page (developers.docusign.com/tools/reference-implementations): connected fields, Data IO, data verification and file output to cloud storage. Each has hosted manifest files that work without running anything locally.
For the optional local run: Git, Node.js and ngrok (or another HTTPS tunnel). Follow the README in the root of the reference implementation repository.
For functional tests: an eSignature template you can edit (connected fields test) and a standalone web form (Data IO workflow test).
Reference code for the API side of connected fields (read only, no credentials): d:/Docusign exam/docusign-node-quickstart/app/lib/connectedFields/examples/setConnectedFields.js.

exercises.title: 1. Read a manifest: connections, extensions, actions
steps: Open the hosted manifest for the connected fields reference implementation (and, if time allows, the Data IO one).
Find the connections array: note name, type oauth2, params.provider CUSTOM, grantType, scopes and customConfig (authorizationUrl, tokenUrl, authorizationMethod, scopeSeparator).
Find extensions: note template and actionReferences.
Find actions: for each, note template, connectionsReference and params.uri.
Draw the links: extension.actionReferences -> action.name; action.connectionsReference -> connection.name.
observe: One manifest = one external platform connection; any number of extensions and actions.
The connected fields extension needs Verify plus the DataIO GetTypeNames and GetTypeDefinitions actions.
grantType is authorization_code or client_credentials; redirect_uri is generated by Docusign and must not be hard-coded.
examTraps: connectionsReference (on actions) points to a connection name; actionReferences (on extensions) point to action names. Do not swap them.
params.uri is where Docusign calls YOUR endpoint (or API proxy); the endpoint must be reachable by Docusign over HTTPS.
If your API does not match the Docusign action contract, add an API proxy instead of rewriting the backend.

exercises.title: 2. Register twice: by editing the manifest vs the form-based experience
steps: Developer Console > Create App > By editing the manifest. Paste or upload the hosted connected fields manifest, give it a unique name (for example Lab6 CF manifest), click Validate, fix errors, Create App.
Create App > Using a form-based experience: app name, published by, support email, distribution type Private, extension Connected Fields (or Data Input Output). Create App.
In the form-based app open Integration Details: edit Connection (client ID, secret, authorization settings) and Extensions & Actions (Params URI per action).
Download the manifest of the form-based app from the kebab menu and compare it with the first one.
Note the App ID and the Draft status on My Extension Apps.
exercises.api: No API call: Developer Console UI (Create App > By editing the manifest / Using a form-based experience).
observe: The manifest editor validates in real time; validation errors block Create App.
The form-based app produces the same manifest structure (you can download it).
A duplicate app name is rejected: each extension app needs a unique name.
New apps start in Draft; statuses are Draft, In Review, Approved, Rejected, Live, Discontinued.
examTraps: Both registration methods produce a manifest; the manifest route is better for copies per environment and source control.
Distribution can be changed only in Draft, Approved or Rejected status, not once Live; publicationRegions can be added later but not removed.
The connection settings support one external environment at a time: switch by editing the registration or keep one registration per environment.

exercises.title: 3. Optional (30-45 min): run the connected fields reference implementation behind ngrok
steps: Clone the connected fields reference implementation and follow its README: install dependencies, set its environment variables, start it locally.
Start ngrok for the local port and copy the https forwarding URL as {yourHost}.
Edit your manifest-based registration: set the authorization and token URLs and each action's params.uri to {yourHost} paths as the README describes; validate and save.
Run the connection and extension tests (exercise 4) against the local app and watch the requests arrive in the local console or the ngrok inspector (http://127.0.0.1:4040).
Restart ngrok (free plan gives a new URL) and see the tests fail until you update the registration.
exercises.api: Docusign -> {yourHost}: OAuth authorize/token calls during the connection test, then POST to each action's params.uri (GetTypeNames, GetTypeDefinitions, Verify) with a JSON body defined by the action contract.
observe: The local app receives Docusign's calls only because ngrok gives it a public HTTPS URL.
Get Type Definitions returns a Concerto data model; properties marked VerifiableType / IsRequiredForVerifyingType control which connected fields appear and which are required.
Changing the external URL means changing the registration (params.uri, auth URLs).
examTraps: Infrastructure question: Docusign must reach your endpoint -> public HTTPS, firewall allow-list or API proxy; a tunnel like ngrok is for development only.
Before submitting a public app for review, the registration must hold production URLs.
Data model changed after connecting -> refresh the connection in the App Center so Docusign re-runs GetTypeNames and GetTypeDefinitions.

exercises.title: 4. Console tests: install, connection test, extension tests
steps: Open the app > App Testing. If the banner says the app is not installed to your developer account, click Install app.
Connection row > Run Test: sign in with the authorization provider credentials (the reference implementation README gives test credentials).
For each extension row (GetTypeNames, GetTypeDefinitions, Verify) > Run Test: check the endpoint URL shown, supply request body values per the action contract, run it and read the response.
Run the connection test a second time and then look at the App Center connections for the app.
exercises.api: Developer Console App Testing: Connection test (OAuth to the external service) -> Extension tests (POST to each params.uri with a contract-shaped body).
observe: Extension tests are disabled until a connection test succeeds: they reuse that authorization.
The endpoint URL on the test page comes from params.uri and cannot be edited there; fix the registration instead.
Registration updates are applied automatically to the installed app; no reinstall is needed.
Repeated connection tests create extra connections, which later show up as duplicate entries in eSignature Add Fields.
examTraps: Integration tests = connection test + extension tests (from the Docusign platform straight to your endpoints); they do not replace functional tests from the extension point.
Extension test fails but connection test passes -> wrong params.uri or a response that does not match the contract (consider an API proxy).
Connected fields missing in Add Fields -> app not installed/connected, or GetTypeNames/GetTypeDefinitions failed (data model error).

exercises.title: 5. Functional test from eSignature: connected fields in an envelope
steps: eSignature > Templates > edit a template > Add Fields > Custom Fields > App Fields > your app.
Drag a required connected field onto the document (the required group is added); in Data Verification tick Must verify to sign.
Save, send an envelope from the template to yourself, open it from the email.
Enter valid values, then invalid ones, then change a value after success.
Optional API view: read setConnectedFields.js to see TabInfo:GetConnectedFieldsTabGroups -> extensionData on each text tab -> Envelopes:create.
exercises.api: UI test. API equivalent: TabInfo:GetConnectedFieldsTabGroups (returns the tabs with extensionData for each installed connected fields app) -> copy extensionData into each tab -> POST {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{accountId}/envelopes.
observe: A Verifying data message appears once all required connected fields are filled, then success or failure.
Invalid values fail verification; with Must verify to sign the signer cannot finish.
Changing a value triggers verification again.
Verification results also show in the envelope history and certificate of completion (and the Connect extension-executed event, JSON SIM only).
examTraps: Connected fields = verify signer-entered data against YOUR system of record during eSignature signing; they are not supported in Maestro.
If only optional connected fields are on the document, verification fails: include the required ones.
After changing the registration, create a new template or envelope (or follow connection best practices) before testing again.

exercises.title: 6. Functional test from Maestro: Data IO read and write
steps: Register the hosted Data IO reference manifest (as in exercise 2), install it and pass the connection test.

Create a workflow: start From within Maestro (manual), one participant, a Read from <app name> step, a Collect Data with Web Forms step (standalone form) and a Write to <app name> step, then Show a Confirmation Screen.
Map the read fields into the form and the form fields into the write step; publish and run one instance.
Check the external store (reference app) for the written record.
exercises.api: UI test. Data IO actions invoked by Maestro: GetTypeNames and GetTypeDefinitions (on connect), SearchRecords (read step), CreateRecord / PatchRecord (write step).
observe: The Read from / Write to step only appears when the app is installed and connected and GetTypeNames/GetTypeDefinitions succeeded.
The objects and fields offered in the step come from GetTypeNames and GetTypeDefinitions.
The form shows values read from the external system; the written record appears there after submit.
examTraps: Read/write a system of record inside a workflow -> Data IO extension (extension point: Maestro workflows).
Store completed agreements in cloud storage from a workflow -> File output to cloud storage (file archive is legacy).
There is no UpdateRecord action: Data IO uses CreateRecord, PatchRecord and SearchRecords.

exercises.title: 7. Distribution and review: private vs public, what is checked
steps: Open App Center Listing in one of your apps: icon, screenshots (up to four), descriptions, publisher, terms/privacy/support URLs, distribution and regions.
Open App Center preview and compare it with the listing data.
Open Publish to App Center and read (do not submit) the review submission steps and the private-sharing screen (production account GUIDs, alias, Pending/Accepted).
Write one line for each: who can install a public app, who can install a private app, what happens when you remove a private app from an account.
exercises.api: No API call: Developer Console (App Center Listing, App Center preview, Publish to App Center).
observe: Review evaluates business, technical, security and functional aspects; you can track or cancel it and resubmit after fixes.
After approval: public apps need one more click to go live in the App Center; private apps need the allowed production account IDs.
Private share status stays Pending until the account admin accepts the app in the App Center, then Accepted.
Removing a private app from an account does not notify its administrator.
examTraps: Verification against one organisation's internal data, or a customer-specific integration -> PRIVATE distribution.
A reusable connector for any customer, listed in the App Center -> PUBLIC (choose publicationRegions).
Lifecycle: register (form or manifest) -> connection + extension tests -> functional tests -> submit for review -> Approved -> publish (public listing or private accounts).
Private apps are shared with production account IDs (GUIDs), not with demo accounts or user emails.

cleanup: Delete the test connections you no longer need in the App Center (duplicates from repeated connection tests).
Delete or leave in Draft the lab extension apps; never submit lab apps for review.
Stop ngrok and the local reference app; remove any test secrets from the manifests you downloaded.
Pause and unpublish the Data IO test workflow; delete the connected fields test template if you will not reuse it.
takeaways: Extension apps bring third-party services INTO Docusign at extension points; API integrations call Docusign from outside.
Connected fields and data verification -> eSignature (email/phone verification also in Web Forms); Data IO and file output -> Maestro workflows.
Manifest = connection(s) + extensions (actionReferences) + actions (connectionsReference, params.uri) + listing metadata + distribution.
Form-based and manifest registration are equivalent; use manifests for per-environment copies.
Integration tests (connection, then extension) before functional tests; fix params.uri in the registration, not on the test page.
Your endpoint must be public HTTPS (or behind an API proxy); ngrok is for development only, production URLs before review.
Private = listed production accounts (org-specific data); Public = all App Center customers in chosen regions.
Review checks business, technical, security and functional aspects; Approved apps still need Publish to App Center.
